title: Rental property owner tax return (Schedule E) document request
use_when: Pick this when the client owns residential rental real estate reported on Schedule E; add the basic individual list for personal items.
note: Built from IRS rental income guidance (Topic 414, Publication 527 and the IRS rental real estate tips page). It covers the income and expense records the IRS describes; state returns and loss limitation forms are not covered.

rental-tips.name: IRS, Tips on rental real estate income, deductions and recordkeeping (web page, last reviewed or updated 04-Apr-2026)

tc414.name: IRS, Topic no. 414, Rental income and expenses (web page, last reviewed or updated 09-Nov-2026)

p463.name: IRS, Publication 463 (2025), Travel, Gift, and Car Expenses, chapter 5 and Table 5-1

situations.advance-rent: Received rent before the period it covers
situations.security-deposit: Holds or kept tenant security deposits
situations.lease-cancel: A tenant paid to cancel a lease
situations.tenant-paid: A tenant paid any of the owner's expenses
situations.barter: Received property or services instead of rent
situations.part-owner: Owns only part of the property
situations.mortgage: Has a mortgage on the rental property
situations.new-rental: Property was bought or first rented recently, or is new to the firm
situations.vehicle: Used a personal vehicle for rental activities
situations.travel: Traveled away from home for the rental property

items.label: Street address of each rental property
Number of days rented at a fair rental price and number of personal-use days, for each property
Ownership percentage, and the client's part of the rental income and expenses
Records of all rent received for each property
Advance rent received
items.detail: Any amount received before the period it covers, in the year received.

items.label: Security deposit records
items.detail: Deposits used as a final payment of rent, and any part kept because the tenant broke the lease or damaged the property.

items.label: Payments received from a tenant for canceling a lease
Owner's expenses paid by the tenant
items.detail: For example a utility bill the tenant paid and deducted from the rent.

items.label: Property or services received instead of rent, with fair market value
Receipts, canceled checks or bills for rental expenses
Expense amounts by type for each property
items.detail: Publication 527 lists the most common: advertising, auto and travel, cleaning and maintenance, commissions, depreciation, insurance, interest (other), legal and other professional fees, local transportation, management fees, mortgage interest paid to banks, points, rental payments, repairs, taxes, utilities.

items.label: Form 1098, Mortgage Interest Statement, or similar statement
items.detail: Publication 527 says one should be received if $600 or more of mortgage interest was paid to any one person. If someone else received the Form 1098, give that person's name and address.

items.label: Insurance premiums paid for more than 1 year in advance, with the period covered
Cost of improvements, kept separate from repairs
items.detail: Include the year of each improvement or added furnishings.

items.label: Purchase price and the settlement fees and closing costs paid when buying the property
items.detail: Publication 527 lists abstract fees, charges for installing utility services, legal fees, recording fees, surveys, transfer taxes, title insurance, and amounts the seller owed that the buyer agreed to pay.

items.label: Date the property was ready and available for rent
Car records for rental activities
items.detail: Mileage for each use, total miles for the year, dates, destination and purpose, following chapter 5 of Publication 463.

items.label: Travel records for trips to collect rent or to manage, conserve or maintain the property
items.detail: Cost of each separate expense, dates left and returned, destination and purpose, following chapter 5 of Publication 463.
